}} The '''Toxic Valley''' is one of the eight [[Fallout 76 locations#Regions|regions]] of [[Appalachia]]. ==Background== The region known to survivors as Toxic Valley lies due north of [[the Forest]], covered by a thin, industrial white powder and filled with filthy, polluted water sources. The [[Grafton Steel]] Mill, sitting amidst the desolation, was the engine driving the economic development of [[Grafton]], the central city of the valley.[[Fallout 76 loading screens|''Fallout 76'' loading screens]]: ''"Grafton Steel Mill was the center of economic development for the town of Grafton, and its large, industrial machines remain relatively intact."'' Grafton entered a steep decline as the pollution from the steel mill ruined the environment and polluted the rivers, while the workers started striking against the creeping automation that was leaving them jobless and their families penniless. The pollution is kept in check by the [[Grafton Dam]]. It was built to provide power to the steel mill and is now filled with the polluted waters of the Toxic Valley.[[Fallout 76 loading screens|''Fallout 76'' loading screens]]: ''"Built to provide power to the Steel Mill, the Grafton Dam is now filled with the polluted waters of the Toxic Valley."'' [[Grafton Lake]] and other deadly waters are home to all manner of mutated, aquatic beasts.[[Fallout 76 loading screens|''Fallout 76'' loading screens]]: ''"The lake and other polluted waters of the Toxic Valley region are home to all manner of mutated, aquatic beasts."'' The area also has a large river that leads to the Grafton Lake. The Toxic Valley contains many points of tourism including [[Clarksburg Shooting Club]], [[Hemlock Holes]], [[Pioneer Scout camp]], and [[Wavy Willard's Water Park]]. == Characteristics == After the Great War, the combined pollution and nuclear fallout filled the white wastes of the Toxic Valley with all manner of horrifying beasts, prowling the stretches of devastated waste in search of the few hardy plants that survived the blight or prey to consume.[[Fallout 76 loading screens|''Fallout 76'' loading screens]]: ''"The region known to survivors as the "Toxic Valley" is covered by industrial white powder and polluted water sources."'' The pale ashen landscape is dry, uneven, and spiked with the barren husks of trees. At night, the ground itself glows in many places, especially along the river. Large herds of radstags can be encountered here. ==Layout== The Toxic Valley is in the northwestern portion of the Appalachia map. Locations in the region include: {{columns|3| {{pagelist|hidens=always|Toxic Valley locations}} }} ==Quests/events== {{columns|2| * TW004 "Daily: [[Big Game Hunter]]" [QUST:0011D76B] * TW010 "Daily: [[Thrill of the Grill]]" [QUST:0023C7F3] * TWZ03 "Daily: [[Target Rich Environment]]" [QUST:001155AF] * TWZ11 "Daily: [[Pass the Buck]]" [QUST:0015B1E2] * TWZ13 "Daily: [[Buried with Honor]]" [QUST:0010C1E3] * TW003 "Event: [[Manhunt]]" [QUST:0010E200] * TW006 "Event: [[Protest March]]" [QUST:0000418B] * TW043 "Event: [[Patrol Duty]]" [QUST:0005A243] * TWZ05 "Event: [[Swarm of Suitors]]" [QUST:0025C090] * TWZ07 "Event: [[Grafton Day]]" [QUST:0025C0F4] * TWZ09 "Event: [[Dogwood Die Off]]" [QUST:00088A9A] }} ==Quotes== {{Quotation|The far northwestern Region of Appalachia is covered in a lightly irradiated blanket of white toxic materials. Much of the landscape (most noticeably the rivers and lakes) is now a choked mess of orange filth and noxious clouds; the environment is unpleasant, rough going, and the tree cover has been ripped away. Now the atmosphere is dead. That's not to say nothing has survived, but the non-robotic entities you'll meet as you visit this stark and unforgiving depression aren't going to be trading anything with you but diseases and savage wounding. As you discover more locations, prepare to visit dilapidated farmsteads, lakeside cabins, and a scout camp where poisonous effluent has replaced clear waters. The main town is Grafton, which is in a rough state, even before reports of its headless monster were confirmed. Seek small respite at the Wavy Willard's Water Park, where there's some frivolity to be had, and ignore the golf course at Hemlock Holes. Instead, spend time cultivating your drive to mine resources at the nearby workshop. There's also tough battles at close quarters with denizens inside the penitentiary along the southern border, a few scattered Raider camps to uncover, and a crashed satellite to the northeast. Finally, pay some respects at the historic sites along the eastern edge of this forsaken region.|''[[Fallout 76 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide]]'' p.353}} {{Quotation|The region known to survivors as “Toxic Valley” is covered by industrial white powder and polluted water sources. The lake and other deadly waters of the Toxic Valley region are home to all manner of mutated, aquatic beasts. Above the fetid lake, Grafton Steel Mill was the center of economic development for the town of Grafton, and its large, industrial machines remain relatively intact. Grafton was built on the shores of the Tygart Valley River. It was a hub for shipping prior to the Great War, thanks to having both water and railroad access. Now it seems deserted and inhospitable. Straddling the boundary between Toxic Valley and the Forest is Grafton Dam. Built to provide power to the Steel Mill, the dam is now filled with the polluted waters of Toxic Valley.|''[[Fallout 76 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide]]''}} ==Appearances== The Toxic Valley appears only in ''[[Fallout 76]]''. ==Behind the scenes== The [[Tygart Valley River]] that runs through the Toxic Valley is based on the real world [[wikipedia:Tygart Valley River|Tygart Valley River]]. ==Gallery== Toxic Valley DOI poster.png|Regional poster ToxicValley-Fallout76.jpg F76 01 welcome to west virginia 002.jpg|''Fallout 76 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide'' FO76 Landscape Toxic Valley.png FO76 Overview of Toxic Valley.png FO76 Toxic valley trees.png FO76 Toxic Valley Overlook.png FO76 Blast zone 17.png|After a nuclear detonation FO76 Blast zone 13.png FO76 Blast zone 10.png 76 region Toxic Valley.jpg Fallout magic Desolate Mire.png|''[[Magic: The Gathering]]'' card Fallout magic Desolate Mire Extended Art.png|Extended Art ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox locations FO76}} [[Category:Toxic Valley locations| ]] [[de:Toxic Valley]] [[es:Valle tóxico]] [[fr:Vallée toxique]] [[it:Valle Tossica (Fallout 76)]] [[pt:Vale Tóxico]] [[ru:Ядовитая долина]] [[uk:Отруєна долина]] [[zh:百毒谷]]

She runs the gun store in [[the Crater]]. Ae-Ri commonly trades in stolen items, especially [[Pipe gun (Fallout 76)|pipe pistols]] and [[Combat knife (Fallout 76)|combat knives]], which she is annoyed to keep getting.Ae-Ri: ''"I'm so tired of these pipe pistols and combat knives. People need to get more interesting shit to steal."''
([[Ae-Ri/Dialogue#25|Ae-Ri's dialogue]]) She is also able to recalibrate scopes.Ae-Ri: ''"Don't let me forget. I gotta recalibrate that scope for [[Surge]]. When someone asks for deadly precision, who am I to let them down?"''
([[Ae-Ri/Dialogue#21|Ae-Ri's dialogue]]) ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions FO76 |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares =[[Wastelanders weapons|Weapons]] |caps =1400 |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started = |quests involved = }} ===Effects of player's actions=== Ae-Ri will remark on the [[Vault Dweller (Fallout 76)|Vault Dweller's]] actions during the [[Fallout 76 quests#Raiders|Raiders questline]]. For example, once [[Cheating Death]] is completed, she will thank the Vault Dweller for saving [[Lucky Lou]]. If [[Vault 79]] is raided with the Raiders, [[Ra-Ra]] mentions Ae-Ri told her that she would make a cool spiky collar for her rabbit doll. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |apparel = [[Leather coat (Fallout 76)|Leather coat]] |weapon = |otheritem = |ondeath = }} ==Appearances== Ae-Ri appears {{In|FO76WL}}. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox vendors FO76}} {{Navbox raiders FO76}} {{Navbox Wastelanders}} [[Category:Wastelanders human characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders raider characters]] [[Category:Wastelanders merchants]] [[Category:Crater Raiders characters]] [[ru:Эй-Ри]]
